The Nigerian Association of Resident Doctors has clarified that it did not issue an ultimatum to the Federal Government over outstanding allowances and other welfare demands, but gave the government four weeks for further engagement. The President of NARD, Dr Ogar Idoko, made the clarification during an interview with Arise News, on Thursday. Idoko said the association’s decision to allow further discussions followed progress recorded on some of its demands since the current leadership assumed office. “We did not serve government any ultimatum. We just gave them four weeks so that we can go back to the drawing board and engage further with them,” he said. He explained that although the association had previously issued ultimatums, its National Executive Council considered continued dialogue more appropriate in view of the progress made. The association is seeking the payment of 14 months’ outstanding professional allowances and promotion arrears before Christmas. Idoko said the Federal Government had paid four months of the 18 months’ outstanding professional allowances following an agreement reached at a tripartite meeting at the Presidential Villa. He also disclosed that more than 400 doctors were yet to receive the 25 to 35 per cent upward review of their allowances because their names were omitted from the initial payment. According to him, NARD had submitted the affected doctors’ details and expected the outstanding payments to be made after the completion of the November salary process. The NARD president appealed to President Bola Tinubu to activate Article 17 of the National Constitution, as amended, to facilitate the payment of the outstanding allowances. He insisted that the payments were not Christmas bonuses but existing entitlements owed to doctors. “It is not a Christmas bonus. It is our due,” he said. The association is expected to review the government’s response on December 20 and determine its next steps if the outstanding issues remain unresolved. The clarification comes days after Idoko commended President Bola Tinubu over the Federal Government’s completion of the payment of the 2026 Medical Residency Training Fund , describing it as a “major achievement in addressing the welfare concerns of doctors”. PUNCH Online had reported that Idoko made the remarks while reading a statement at a briefing at NARD’s secretariat in Abuja on Thursday, following the association’s Extraordinary National Executive Council meeting. The association also praised the Federal Government for approving an upward review of the fund for 2027 and commencing payment of outstanding Professional Allowance Table arrears, with four of the 18 months owed to healthcare workers already paid.
